newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end off day's lows, slump to continue.
newsitem.headline: India shares end off day's lows, slump to continue.

text.p: A crash in Indian shares dragging stock markets to three-year lows showed some signs of halting on Wednesday, but brokers and analysts said the selling spree would continue for some time on the back of a bearish sentiment.
"More of delivery-based selling is pushing down prices..the retail investors waiting to sell are getting desperate," analyst Nikhil Vora at Ceat Financial Services told Reuters.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index plunged 85 points, or 3.0 percent in mid-session, but recovered slightly to end at 2,754.06, down 52.94 points over Tuesday's close.
"It looks as if this fall was expected...we might now see some good values in the market at these levels," said Vora.
Traders said some short-covering in front-bencher stocks and buying from local funds stemmed the market's sharp fall on Wednesday, but the outlook remained pessimistic.
"We feel there might be support around the 2,700 level, but it will only be short-lived," said chief dealer S Ramakrishnan at ASK-Raymond James Securities India Ltd.
A bearish sentiment led to nervous market conditions, with major players also jumping onto the selling bandwagon.
India's overseas listed shares plummetted in London in panicky trade on Wednesday. The James Capel index for Indian GDRs fell 2.71 points, or 4.9 percent, to 52.07 points in afternoon trade.
"There are many red signals out on the economic front..people are pressing sales in infrastructure stocks," he said.
Ceat Financial's Vora said commodity stocks had taken a sharp hit in the recent fall in share prices.
"Cement, steel, petrochemicals..are not on the buy list of any firms," he said.
"Correct values for stocks are now being built in..there was too much hype about the cement story," Vora added.
Gujarat Ambuja Cement which bore the brunt of selling pressure in recent sessions ended 4.24 rupees higher at 195.25.
Auto stocks Mahindra & Mahindra and TELCO closed slightly higher.
The Bombay index has dived 145.44 points, or 5.03 percent, this week from last Friday's close of 2,890.50.
